youtube.title: Two Pizzas or One? Everyone Gets It Wrong #Shorts
youtube.description:
Lucas ordered two pizzas. Amira ordered one. She got more pizza.

Pizza is a surface: area grows with the square of the width, so twice as wide means four times the pizza. One 18-inch pizza is about 254 square inches; two 12-inch pizzas are about 226. Studies on size judgement suggest we compare one dimension and don't adjust enough for the other (Krider, Raghubir & Krishna, 2001; Ordabayeva & Chandon, 2013). And in NPR's analysis of 74,476 pizza prices, bigger pies were usually cheaper per square inch.

So, would you still order two?

Sources:
- NPR Planet Money (2014), 74,476 Reasons You Should Always Get The Bigger Pizza: https://www.npr.org/sections/money/2014/02/26/282132576/74-476-reasons-you-should-always-get-the-bigger-pizza
- Krider, Raghubir & Krishna (2001), Pizzas: pi or square? Psychophysical biases in area comparisons, Marketing Science 20(4): https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mksc.20.4.405.9756
- Ordabayeva & Chandon (2013), Predicting and managing consumers' package size impressions, Journal of Marketing 77(5): https://pure.eur.nl/en/publications/predicting-and-managing-consumers-package-size-impressions/

Lucas, Amira and the pizzeria are fictional.
